review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed inspection to submission; includes coordination/tool delays, not independent human labor.

anchors.quote: Conditionally encode the row indices from col through n-1 as a finite search domain. Mark an index i exactly when abs(rows[i][col]) is strictly greater than every earlier candidate value and at least every later candidate value, thereby reproducing Python max's first-index tie rule. A Grover-style procedure would only propose the uniquely marked pivot index.

Encode col, candidate indices, and the dynamically updated binary64 values rows[i][col]. The reversible oracle must reproduce the relevant Python floating-point absolute-value, comparison, equality, signed-zero, and ordering behavior, including behavior if elimination has produced nonfinite intermediate values. Coherent data loading, value representation, ancilla cleanup, and their resource costs are unresolved.

Measure a proposed row index and classically verify that it is exactly the first index selected by Python's argmax over abs(rows[i][col]). On failed search or verification, execute the original classical max expression. Preserve the following zero-pivot check, row swap, elimination, back substitution, overflow handling, and report construction unchanged.

binding.rationale: Explicit primary rule requires strict greater-than against earlier values and at least every later value. Bind the conventional >= reading of at least. Dynamic nonfinite states are discussed without an admission exclusion, so guard True. Classical fallback is separate and does not repair the marked-state relation.

interpretations.meaning: Earlier strict-greater and later nonstrict-greater comparisons.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i) and all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices if k > i)
